changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers: offer to cost their month-end close from one month of their own statements and staff costs, including hours of manual matching and write-offs on deposits never matched, so the figure is theirs and not ours. Suggested line: "We'll build the cost of your close from your own statements. Your number, not ours."
changes.why: The deal was at 20 percent until a cost model built from the controller's own statements produced a figure the CFO accepted as "my number, not yours.", which is the opposite of an independent-study claim.

changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers, open the first call with reconciliation in the customer's words: "Know where every deposit came from, matched to its transactions and invoices in your ERP, and close the month without the archaeology." Offer to show it on their own data.
changes.why: Payout reconciliation was the only part of the pitch that got a reaction, and the CFO asked to see it on her own data; she framed the problem as "I just want to know where my money is." and "month-end is a week of archaeology.", and spoke of "the deposits" rather than payments.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Don't lead with the developer story on first calls where the IT team isn't building anything (for example, an off-the-shelf portal with a plugin). Keep API and sandbox detail behind the finance outcome.
changes.why: The rep ran the standard deck and "the developer story went nowhere" because the IT team of four wasn't building anything.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For distributor and wholesale buyers, lead proof with a peer from the same business model and an invoice-reconciliation story, not a retail case study. Until we have one, don't offer retail stories as peer proof to these buyers. Flag this to customer marketing as a reference gap.
changes.why: The CFO wanted to talk to another distributor, the retail case study was dismissed with "this is a company that sells sweaters.", and she raised the missing reference twice before signing.
